name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+19 district lean plus a Republican-favorable national environment
Incumbent Clay Fuller renominated; prediction markets price Democrats near 4%
Shawn Harris's $8M haul is largely spent, with almost no cash left and outside money heavily favoring Fuller
model.rationale: A nineteen-point Republican lean, a renominated incumbent, and a favorable environment all point the same direction, and prediction markets agree at roughly 96% Republican. Harris's eye-catching fundraising is mostly spent and outside spending backs Fuller heavily, so it is unlikely to close a structural gap this wide.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending, fresh polling showing Harris within single digits, or an unexpected Fuller misstep would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
GA-14 covers deep northwest Georgia, a district that leans about nineteen points Republican, and incumbent Clay Fuller is running for another term after renomination. No public general-election polls are available here, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets. Polymarket traders give the Democrat roughly a four percent chance, consistent with the district's strong Republican tilt and a national environment favoring the GOP.

Democrat Shawn Harris has raised about eight million dollars, far outpacing Fuller's one-point-eight million, a striking total for this terrain. But Harris ends with almost no cash on hand, while outside groups have spent heavily to back Fuller and comparatively little against him. Big Democratic fundraising alone has rarely closed gaps this size in comparable districts, and Fuller remains a strong favorite.
